Illegal Chicken Abattoirs

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We go on a raid with the SPCA to the abandoned buildings in Johannesburg's CBD to catch those responsible for illegal abattoirs (animal cruelty and the health hazard).

Unique Selling Point:
It's a raid!!! So action visuals - we have lots of other visuals from previous investigations showing what we'll find. We will go in 3 different times to maximize our success. The JMPD and Department of Health with be with us to make arrests. The SPCA says this is a problem in Johannesburg because of the number of abandoned buildings, and those living in them kill these animals in basements - filled with hundreds of chickens, abattoir machinery, cooking pots, slaughter areas. These are illegal - the way in which the animals are housed, kept and killed and they do not comply with health regulations with regards to supplying food for consumption. I already have footage of the abandoned buildings so you can see the living conditions.

Summary:
Sandton SPCA raids illegal chicken abattoir in Hillbrow - we will interview Jaco Pieterse. He has been with the SPCA since 2005, and had done many raids before. He believes this is a big problem and has the potential to cause illness in the small cramped, already unclean areas. There is often no oxygen and from the photo's and video's provided it's a health hazard from an animal disease point of view, and from a living conditions point of view. My idea is to speak to the public prosecutor of johannesburg, Adv. Futshane who says we need to prosecute more of these cases, we will also talk to the health department safety inspector on site. The state veterinary services is meant to also be there, but the SPCA says they are not pulling their weight and doing their jobs. If they are there, they will face tough questions as to why they haven't done anything, the SPCA have issued many warnings. And if they aren't there, they will face hard questions about why they aren't even doing their basic investigations.


Further information:
As an example of what we will likely see: https://sandtonchronicle.co.za/190645/sandton-spca-raid-illegal-chicken-abattoir-hillbrow/

We will need extra lights for the darkness

Press Release:


Illegal Chicken Abattoir
Blood on the floors and rats – that was the scene in the basement of an apartment building in downtown Johannesburg. It’s under these conditions that hundreds of broiler chickens are slaughtered in this illegal chicken abattoir before they’re packaged and sold to unsuspecting consumers. Carte Blanche joined the Sandton SPCA as it raided the building and rescued these distressed animals.
Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli
Watch the trailer


Script:


Johannesburg City is known as the City of gold - but beneath its streets a seedy underbelly has remained hidden. This is NOT the set of horror movie, but a basement in the inner-city suburb of Yeoville that is being used as an illegal abattoir; and a makeshift kitchen. The men working here slaughter chickens on a bloody tree stump…and provide the ready-to-cook produce for unsuspecting buyers outside on the city’s streets.
MAC: IT BEGAN TWO YEARS AGO WITH A CALL FROM RESIDENTS IN THIS NEIGHBORHOOD TO COMPLAIN ABOUT THE SMELL COMING FROM THAT BASEMENT. SPCA INSPECTORS CAME OUT AND WERE SHOCKED AT WHAT THEY FOUND.
Jaco: We’ve actually raided this particular abattoir with the city of johannesburg’s officials in the past.”
Jaco Pieterse, the Sandton General Manager for the SPCA, says these slaughter houses are hidden around the city. The mass butchery of animals for public consumption is illegal without a licence that regulates everything from hygiene to animal welfare. The SPCA served warnings to this operator in March this year -- but were disappointed by the lack of enforcement by the City’s environmental health department.
Jaco: “We contacted the mayor of the city of joburg in order to discuss the way forward, the mayor then appointed the director of the environmental health department to assist us.”
Director of the City’s environmental health department Peter Manganye promised Pieterse he would take care of everything.
Mac: “Were they all there when you went to the raid?
Jaco: Sadly they were not.”
At the Yeoville police station, Pieterse called Manganye’s secretary who said she had no knowledge of the sting.
Jaco on phone: “He promised that he would have the health inspectors, state vet and JMPD here. He was instructed by the mayor! No one has arrived.”
With warrant in hand Pieterse was determined -- he’d cancelled raids before to wait for the city’s participation.
These street vendors supply live chickens - we saw them crammed into stacked cages with no space to move – some sitting on top of one another.
Jaco: “There you can see there’s no water for these animals, these buckets are dry dry dry, this is in contravention of the law.”
The SPCA lead the way.
Jaco: “We are going to go into the basement and see what else is down there.”
As we enter, the stench of blood and decay assaults our nostrils. A full scale operation was underway on several tables – with proper abattoir machinery.
Jaco: “As you can see there’s no ventilation in here, and the smell, it’s overwhelming in here. One can hardly breathe in here, really it’s. This is no condition for any animal or human to live in.”
The chickens had filthy water and were kept in SEVERAL confined cement rooms. Some had been trampled to death. Our horror only increased as we realised there were hundreds of chickens - all meant to be sold and consumed.
Jaco: “So what these are is to take the feathers off, they throw them in boiling warm water, and then chuck them in here and the machine takes the feathers off. But why don’t you ask him?
Worker2: “We start by killing the chicken With Knife, after that we put them in water-boiled water.”
Sasha: “How much is it per day?”
Worker: “Per Chicken? Its 130,110.”
Sasha: “How much are you paid a day?”
Worker: “A hundred.”
We found buckets filled with what smelled like urine… couches nearby, a snooker table and even a jukebox machine. Another butcher said he lived here.
Sasha: “And you were slaughtering the chickens?”
Worker 1: “Yes, cutting, cutting, cutting. That’s my house right here, and I’m working right here.”
As we investigated, the rats crawled out to greet us.
We found undisposed chicken waste, and even dead chickens in dustbins.
Electrical wires dangled everywhere!
It defies belief that it’s on these feather-and-blood soaked floors that chicken is cooked and then sold on to the unsuspecting public.
Sinethemba: “How many chickens do you do a day?”
Worker: Sometime 50 or 40, but its according to business. Sometimes the customers take 10, 5 or 2 chickens.”
Even just based on what the butchers said they sold per day this enterprise could net up to R130,000 per month. The Gauteng Department of Agriculture and Rural Development's Dr. Dietana Nemud-ziv-hadi is the State Veterinarian in charge of abattoirs.
Dietana: “They are operating in an unregistered facility. An equivalent and abattoir the inside of it, has to look almost like a hospital.”
Mac: And these look nothing like a hospital!
Dietana: “That in itself puts a risk of contamination of that product that is going to be produced from there.”
Dr. Nemud-ziv-hadi says the certification criteria in the Meat Safety Act requires an abattoir to provide:
adequate care for the animals;
a hygiene management system for employees;
qualified personnel wearing protective clothing;
controlled disposal of waste;
And inspections prior, during and post slaughter.
Mac: “The only Inspectors that we found there were rats!
Dietana: “Rats are associated with whole bunch of pathogens like salmonella, our registration process requires that they should have a rodent control.”
Jaco meeting police: “We want to arrest the workers, for operating an illegal abattoir, for cruelty to animals, for contravention of the health bylaws.”
But as the police rounded them up, they escaped.
Disappointed, Pietese issued marching orders.
Jaco: “So the plan of action is that we are going to load these other crates on the back of the trailer.”
Then the City’s health inspector finally arrived.
Jaco showing inspector: “If I can just show you here quickly...”
Hundreds of chickens were packed into several vans, and the abattoir equipment was confiscated. The SPCAs Vet Dr. Rene Smit checked the animals upon arrival.
Vet: “I’m just looking for any fractures of the wings, severe bruising, cuts that infected already, abscess or anything like that.
These chickens are broiler hens.
Jaco: “Their main purpose is to be fed, and fattened up as quickly as possible. And we’re talking about in a few weeks time, these chickens are from a chick, raised to an adult to be slaughtered for meat. These chickens grow so quickly because of the hormones that are added into the food, that their legs aren’t able to carry their body weight.”
Vet: “The ones that are cruel to keep alive those are the ones that we decide to euthanize.”
The survivors were finally released into pens in the sunshine.
Jaco: “This is the first time the majority of these chickens have experienced any kindness or dignity in their life, in the short span that they’ve been alive. As you can see they enjoying the hay and the grass, this is actually the first time their feet touched soil. Now imagine how these animals must have felt inside there, it’s not conducive for any living creature to live in a basement like that.”
Peter: “Ongoing monitoring of a premises for hygiene purposes in the city of johannesburg, is the function of environmental health. Where illegal activities is observed by an inspector, we are responsible for public health bylaws.”
Mac: “Are they being broken here?”
Peter: “The cities bylaws are broken completely in this instance.”
Mac: “It’s the second time a raid is being done on this place, which means they’re not being monitored as well.”
Peter: “We raid a place, it gets quiet and then a few months down the line it resurfaces.”
A few months? Try days, Director!
Dietana: “My team of veterinarians paid a visit to this facility to their horror and surprise it was business as usual.”
Peter: “I checked up with the office this morning, and I checked up that it’s not operating.”
Mac: “The GDARD team went back again yesterday, it’s still operating...
Peter: “I think it requires constant monitoring and vigilance.”
We visited the basement after the interview, to see for ourselves.

MAC: LINK - WE HAD HOPED IT WOULD HAVE BEEN SHUT DOWN, BUT IT’S BUSINESS AS USUAL.

At least 50 chickens were back in cages, now patched up, and the same team was back at work.
UPSOUND TO COME
Mac: “I won’t take you seriously if every single time you leave business carries on.”
Peter: “We will go and check, this time I’ll make sure I go and join them.”
There are many diseases associated with eating unhygienic chicken.
Dietana: “A whole list, e coli, one of the top ones. Superbugs resistant to antibiotics, campylobacter, salmonella, listeria… those top 4. If you’re not sure… mhmh (shakes head) rather not.”
Dr. Nemud-ziv-hadi says their solution is in having - mobile abattoirs - allowing for the safe and hygienic slaughter of animals.
SPCA: “The city is definitely failing its citizens if they allow this chicken abattoir to continue, they allow… ppl should not be consuming that meat.”
Peter: “My participation in raids is an ongoing kind of participating, it’s unfortunate, that I missed just this one.”
Mac: You can also do better?
Peter: “We can tighten up on issues of hygiene and breaking of our own bylaws.”
Mac: “We’ll hold you to it.”
Peter: “Definitely.”
We visited the chickens 5 days after their rescue.
MACFARLANE: THE OWNER HAS A WEEK TO CLAIM THE CHICKENS, AND IF HE DOESN’T THEY WILL BE PUT UP FOR ADOPTION FROM THE SANDTON SPCA. WHY DID THE CHICKEN CROSS THE ROAD – NOT TO END UP ON THE PLATE.

The state veterinary services is meant to also be there, but the SPCA says they are not pulling their weight and doing their jobs. If they are there, they will face tough questions as to why they haven't done anything, the SPCA have issued many warnings. And if they aren't there, they will face hard questions about why they aren't even doing their basic investigations.
